tests.title: Smoothing the stair-steps: anti-aliasing at the full-screen default
tests.when: After the brick build finishes. About 3 min to build, 13 min to run; leave the Mac alone.
tests.what: Since full screen went to 2048x1152 without dynamic resolution, the camera has no anti-aliasing at all (STP used to do it), so thin edges stair-step. This compares FXAA, SMAA (high), TAA (high, sharpened), STP as pure anti-aliasing at 100%, and a 2560x1440 backbuffer with TAA or SMAA, with FPS on every tile. The same run splits the night transparent cost (foyer and hall: all transparents off gained 10-19 ms though glass and sheers cost nothing) into its HDRP passes.
look: Each tile has the frame and two or three edge patches magnified 2x: roof lines and branches at the piers, the eaves at night, the balusters, handrail and mirror in the foyer.
Look for smooth edges without blur or shimmer: TAA and STP smooth the most but can soften wallpaper and brick; FXAA is cheapest and softest on text-like detail; SMAA keeps texture sharp.
Keep an eye on FPS: the pick must keep 30 fps at the foyer and hall at night.
The off=... columns are cost readings for the transparent pass, not looks.
tests.app: HomeAlonePerfAA.app, full screen on the Studio Display (2048x1152 default; lamp ranges fitted to rooms)
commands: HA_PERF_APP=$HOME/.cache/home-alone-perf/build/HomeAlonePerfAA.app HA_DISPLAY="Studio Display" HA_PERF_ARGS='-perfab -perfrounds 1 -perfbasescale auto -perfposes piers-day,street-night,foyer-night,hall-night -perfvariants aa=fxaa;aa=smaa;aa=taa;aa=stp;screen=2560x1440+aa=taa;screen=2560x1440+aa=smaa;off=TransparentPrepass;off=TransparentPostpass;off=LowResTransparent;off=Refraction;off=Distortion;off=TransparentsWriteMotionVector;off=TransparentSSR;off=LensFlareDataDriven' tools/house/perf_probe.sh run fs-aa

tests.title: Night speed: what's expensive in the foyer, kitchen and hall
tests.when: Settled: you kept the lamp range fitted to each room + 1 m (fit=1). It ships in every build from now on (LampFit.cs, applied at load).
tests.what: At the new full-screen default (2048x1152, no dynamic resolution) the night rooms ran 23-29 fps. The biggest win that keeps the look is fitting each lamp's light range to its own room plus 1 m: foyer 23 -> 36, hall 29 -> 45, kitchen 26 -> 32, all over 30. Fog, reflections, ambient occlusion, glass and sheers cost almost nothing. The foyer mirror costs about 20% in the foyer and kitchen. Recommendation: ship 'lamp range fitted to room'.

tests.title: Front brick: upstairs darker than downstairs
tests.when: Prepared, not built. Next: one full build + bake (about 40 min, Mac busy) after your perf test, on the coordinator's go.
tests.what: Your catch, now measured: tools/house/brick_storeys.py compares the upstairs brick with the ground-floor brick at your 06:45 spot (gate: within 5%). NB8 fails every tile: overcast upstairs 0.71 of downstairs in the centre, 0.78 at the left wing; night 0.63 in the centre; sunny 0.95. Cause: every probe outside the rooms is switched off, so the front wall takes its stored light from the rooms behind it, and upstairs that is Marina's bigger, dark upstairs. Fix prepared (BakeLighting): probes outside the film's house stay on and are tagged Exterior, rooms Interior, Marina's strip both; outside walls read only Exterior probes, room surfaces only Interior ones (Unity 6 probe rendering layers), so rooms should not change. Caveat: with the stored light off entirely the upstairs is still 0.81-0.85 of downstairs on our tile (film 6399: 0.94-1.10), so something besides the probes may remain.
look: Until the build: nothing new. The sheet below is the before.
After: upstairs and downstairs brick the same red as in film 6399, by day and at night.
Foyer and living room at night must look unchanged.

tests.title: Full-screen speed: why the Studio Display was slow
tests.what: Lowering the internal resolution (dynamic resolution) was itself the main cost: it stalled the graphics driver for most of each frame. The new default is full screen at a fixed 2048x1152, stretched to the display, with dynamic resolution off; P steps screen sizes. It runs in the next build.
